nfl.vote_outcome_model.mechanism: Winner or rank probability from candidate quality, narrative, previous votes, timing and electorate composition, aggregated through each award's actual ballot, which is a PARAMETER of the model per award and season: voters V, places K and points vector w. AP ballot parameters per award and season, each with its evidence status. (a) MVP, 2025 season: 50 voters, 5 places, points 10-5-3-2-1; seen in search-result copies of AP wire text, AP primary page not fetched. (b) MVP, 2023 season: 5 places, points 10-5-3-2-1 (a per-position tally such as 49-0-1-0-0=493 was seen in a search copy); primary not fetched. (c) The other seven AP awards, 2025 season: 5 places, points 10-5-3-2-1, 50-voter panel; seen in search-result copies of the AP finalist and results text, primary not fetched. (d) MVP from 2022 as a top-5 ballot with only the top three places for the other awards (5-3-1): reported in search copies of an AP statement, UNVERIFIED, and the season in which the non-MVP awards moved to five places is unknown. (e) Single first-place vote before 2022: UNVERIFIED. (f) Voter count for seasons other than 2025, the tie rule and the ballot close date: not found. (g) The tally Stafford 366 points / 24 firsts versus Maye 361 / 23 is reported in search copies as the 2025-season MVP result; the page date of one cited URL was ambiguous, so the season attribution is unconfirmed.
nfl.vote_outcome_model.measurement: Per AP award, model each voter's ranked ballot: rank-ordered (exploded) logit of candidate placements on features (team win% at ballot close, statistical rank within position by EPA or season totals, prior award wins, position dummy), ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV, prior weight 3 pseudo-observations; fit seasons whose full AP placement counts are published, with K, V and w read per award and season from the ballot-parameter table in the mechanism (not hard-coded) and any single-vote seasons on first-place votes only as a separate regime sharing feature weights through a hierarchical prior. Simulate V ballots per draw (V=50 is seen in search copies for 2025 only) and score each with the points vector w of that award-season (10-5-3-2-1 seen in search copies for the MVP and, in 2025, the other AP awards; any other scheme is read from that season's AP tally), winner = highest points (ties shared). Non-AP processes (PFWA Executive of the Year, Hall of Fame, All-Pro, T100) keep their own model: T100 ordered logit on previous rank, change in production, position group, age. Output P(candidate=winner) and P(rank=r); group markets P(group) = sum of P(win) by team at announcement time with 1/N co-winner payout; Executive of the Year tie probability = own-award co-winner frequency shrunk to comparable awards with weight 10. As-of ballot close.

nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.rationale: AP awards are ranked-points ballots (MVP 10-5-3-2-1 over five places and, in 2025, the other AP awards too, all seen in search-result copies with the AP primary page not fetched; earlier non-MVP schemes are reported but unverified), so two similar candidates split first places but not all support: a candidate can win on second- and third-place points (reported in search copies as the 2025 MVP tally: Stafford 366 points with 24 firsts, Maye 361 with 23; season attribution unconfirmed). A penalty fitted to first-place shares under plurality overstates the split for ranked seasons and must be estimated by regime.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.measurement: Rank-ordered logit latent utility for candidate i on voter ballot = x_i'theta - beta_r x max over same-team or same-position rivals j of x_j'theta, where x are the nfl.vote_outcome_model features and r indexes the placement (first place versus lower places). Estimate theta and beta_r by maximum likelihood on placement counts per candidate for seasons with published AP placement counts, with places K and points w read per award and season (see the ballot-parameter table in nfl.vote_outcome_model; evidence status per parameter is explicit there), and on first-place vote shares under a Dirichlet-multinomial for 2005-2021 single-vote seasons as a separate regime; ridge penalty by leave-one-season-out CV, shrink beta_r toward 0. Output winner probabilities from simulated V-voter ballots scored by that award-season's points vector. As-of ballot close.

nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.rationale: Both contracts are low-rate Bernoulli events whose base rate differs strongly by coach and personnel (for example a former-quarterback receiver, or a team that favours quarterback sneaks at the 1; both are hypotheses to test, not measured facts); league averages mislead, but team samples are tiny, so heavy shrinkage toward the league rate is essential and stakes may raise trick-play frequency.
nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.measurement: Non-QB pass: count of pass attempts by players whose roster position is not QB per team-game over the last 3 seasons, shrunk to league rate (about 0.15 per game, to recompute) with k=40 team-games, coach random effect; P(any in game) = 1 - exp(-(rate_A + rate_B)). Pass from the 1: expected snaps with yardline_100 <= 1 per team-game (from drives reaching the 1, last 2 seasons, shrink k=30) x team pass share on those snaps (shrink to league about 0.35 with k=25 snaps) counting official forward pass attempts only; sacks, scrambles and runs must be excluded explicitly (whether the nflverse pass_attempt flag already excludes sacks, how no_play rows are treated and how spikes are flagged are UNVERIFIED); P(at least one) by Poisson. As-of kickoff with the active roster.

nfl.script.mechanism: Teams pass more and play faster when trailing and run and slow down when leading; the expected game script from the own-model expected margin (not the betting spread) therefore determines volume splits between passing and rushing props.
nfl.script.measurement: From play_by_play estimate pass rate, seconds/play, rush attempts and efficiency as a function of score differential bins and time remaining; simulate or integrate with the distribution of game states implied by the market-free margin and total distributions of nfl.model_team_points_mean and nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd (e.g., a Gaussian or t margin around the own-model mean margin); betting spreads and totals are not used; team-specific slope with shrinkage to league.

nfl.weekly_slate_composition.mechanism: Which teams and games are in the week's slate: byes remove teams, Week 18 includes all 32, and international or Thursday games are part of the same week; the game count N of the slate is the exposure of weekly count and maximum contracts.

nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.measurement: Do not build a separate simulator: use the single shared season simulator nfl.standings_sim (with the shared rating-uncertainty draw and tie probability of the win-totals record, 0.25 percent per game and rating prior sd of 4.0 points as the shared assumptions) run on REMAINING games only, conditioned on the results already played as of the current week (completed scores, ties, each team's current win streak and undefeated flag, banked ties), current injuries and quarterback status. For each of 100,000 runs record: the longest streak (under both tie treatments, see u2) for each team, the week of each team's first loss (ties not losses; same-week first losses tied), season tie count (banked + simulated), and the worst-to-first indicator; output probabilities for each contract rung.
